faq.q1: How does the 2% success fee work?
faq.a1: When an investor marks a deal as closed, we invoice the startup for 2% of the amount raised — after closing. 14-day payment window via Stripe. Zero upfront fees.
faq.a2: We're waiving subscription fees entirely for our first 100 members. Everyone gets full access to the top tier at no cost. Once we hit 100 members, regular pricing kicks in for new signups.
faq.q3: Can I cancel my subscription anytime?
faq.a3: Yes. Cancel from your dashboard via the Stripe Customer Portal at any time. You retain access until the end of your billing period.
faq.q4: What counts as a 'closed deal' for the 2% fee?
faq.a4: A deal is closed when both parties confirm the investment was completed through a CapitalReach connection. We don't charge for deals made outside the platform.
faq.q5: Do investors pay the success fee?
faq.a5: No. The 2% fee is charged only to startups. Investors pay zero transaction fees.
faq.a6: Investors must self-certify as accredited to access financial data. CapitalReach stores this certification and may request documentation for institutional accounts.

about.metaDesc: Learn about CapitalReach — our mission, team, and why we built the platform.
about.heroSub: CapitalReach is the private marketplace where vetted early-stage startups connect with serious investors — powered by AI and aligned incentives.
about.missionTitle: Fix the broken connection between great ideas and patient capital
about.missionP1: Most fundraising is opaque, relationship-dependent, and painfully slow. Great founders with real traction get passed over because they don't know the right people. Investors miss obvious opportunities because the deal flow is noisy and unfiltered.
about.missionP2: CapitalReach solves this by building curated infrastructure: every startup is reviewed, every investor is verified, and AI does the heavy lifting of matching. We make money only when deals close — so our incentives are perfectly aligned with yours.
about.v1Desc: We charge the startup 2% — only when a deal closes. Investors pay nothing. Your success is our success.
about.v2Desc: Every startup is manually reviewed before going live. We'd rather have fewer, better listings than a crowded directory.
about.v3Desc: From matching to due diligence, we use AI to remove friction — not to replace human judgment.
about.v4Desc: We were founders first. We build for the version of ourselves that needed this five years ago.

privacy.s1l2: Profile data:|||Company name, tagline, description, industry, stage, funding details, team information, financial metrics, and documents (startups); investment thesis, check size preferences, industries, and portfolio information (investors).

privacy.s2l2: To process payments and subscriptions through Stripe.

privacy.s3l2: With service providers:|||We use Supabase (database/auth), Stripe (payments), Resend (email), OpenAI (AI features), Upstash (rate limiting), and Vercel (hosting). Each provider processes only the data necessary for their service and is bound by data processing agreements.

When you use these features, relevant portions of your profile data are sent to OpenAI for processing. OpenAI's {link} governs how OpenAI handles this data. We use the API (not ChatGPT), meaning your data is not used to train OpenAI's models by default.
privacy.s8Text: We implement industry-standard security measures including TLS encryption in transit, Row Level Security (RLS) in our database so users can only access their own data, and Stripe's PCI-compliant payment processing. However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure. We encourage you to use a strong, unique password and to contact us immediately at {link} if you suspect unauthorized access to your account.
privacy.s9Text: CapitalReach is not intended for users under 18 years of age. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact us and we will delete it promptly.

By using our Service, you consent to these transfers. We ensure appropriate safeguards are in place for international transfers.

privacy.cookiesIntro: We set no advertising or analytics cookies, and load no third-party tracking script. Three things are stored in your browser, all of them to make the site work:

privacy.cookiesLocale: A language cookie (cr_locale) remembering which of the 15 languages you chose.
privacy.cookiesLocal: Local storage for preferences you set yourself — list or board view, your recent searches, your comparison list, and an automatic backup of a listing you are part-way through editing. None of it leaves your device.

glossary.aiScore: A 0–100 estimate of how ready a round looks — how complete the listing is, how much traction is evidenced, and how coherent the numbers are. It is generated by a model from what the founder published. It is not a rating of the company, not investment advice, and no human at CapitalReach has reviewed it.
glossary.aiMatching: Ranks live rounds against the thesis on your profile — stage, sector, cheque size and geography — so the ones worth your time come first. It reads only what founders have published.
glossary.aiDiligence: A structured report a model writes from the listing and any documents the founder shared: what stands out, what is missing, and the questions worth asking. A starting point for your own diligence, never a substitute for it.
glossary.nda: A non-disclosure agreement. The founder can require one before sharing financials or documents; you sign it in-platform and the signature is recorded on the deal.
glossary.scorecard: Your own scoring criteria — team, market, traction, whatever you weigh — applied to a company so two opportunities can be compared on the same basis instead of on how you felt that day.
glossary.savedSearch: A set of filters kept as a standing search. When a new round matches it, you are told, rather than having to check.
glossary.coInvestor: Whether other investors have declared interest in the same round. Founders choose to reveal this per deal; nobody's identity is shared without them opting in.
glossary.allocation: How much of the capital you planned to deploy this period you have actually committed. Set a target and the dashboard shows the gap.
glossary.investorIdentity: On a free plan, interest arrives anonymously. On a paid plan you see which investor it is, so you can decide whether to spend time on the conversation.
glossary.externalContacts: Investors you know off-platform. You can add them to your pipeline and track the conversation here without them having an account. They stay private to you and never appear in the public directory.
glossary.dataRoom: Request specific documents from an investor, or share yours, and see what has been opened and when — instead of a folder link you cannot audit.
glossary.priorityReview: Your listing goes to the front of the review queue when you submit it, rather than being reviewed in the order it arrived.
glossary.mrr: Monthly recurring revenue — the predictable revenue the company bills every month. It excludes one-off payments.
glossary.arr: Annual recurring revenue, usually MRR × 12. A forward-looking run rate, not last year's takings.
glossary.runway: How many months the company can keep operating at its current burn before it runs out of cash.
glossary.preMoney: What the company is agreed to be worth before the new investment lands. Post-money is that plus the money raised.
glossary.safe: A Simple Agreement for Future Equity: money now, shares later, converted at the next priced round — usually with a cap, a discount, or both.
glossary.softCircle: An investor has said they intend to invest, and how much, but nothing is signed. Real interest, not committed money.
glossary.leadInvestor: The investor who sets the terms and usually takes the largest cheque. Rounds often stall until one exists.
glossary.successFee: CapitalReach charges 2% of a round when it closes. It is paid by the startup receiving the investment — never by the investor.
glossary.dueDiligence: The investigation an investor runs before committing money: reading the financials, talking to customers, checking the claims on the listing against evidence. Expect document requests and questions — a diligence that finds nothing to ask about has not started.
glossary.termSheet: The document that fixes the terms of the investment — amount, valuation, rights — before the final contracts. Usually not legally binding on the money itself, but signing one means the negotiation is over and the lawyers begin.
